narrative.overview:
PK-Hub is printed like a Pakistani stamp paper or banknote: an intaglio-green shell framing pale security-print ground, with near-white sheets laid on it and ruled in green-grey hairlines. Each scrape is issued as a numbered document. It gets a serial set in mono, a denomination (the counts it found) and a validation (the badge turns from red to green when it completes). Guilloché linework is the world's one ornament. It appears in exactly three places: the seal mark, the rosette that draws one ring per page read, and the engraved edge of the rail.

The console is dense and works at office-desktop distance. Forms, run sheets and results tables sit at full width with hairline rules rather than heavy cards, and counts are set at poster scale so you can read a run's progress from across the room. Colour is used sparingly and has a job. Green means the shell and the committing action. Serial red means a run is in flight right now. Ochre is the dark rail's accent. Everything else is green-tinted ink on paper.

The world rejects the category default of white cards, a grey canvas and a single blue accent. It also rejects the navy-and-gold look it replaced.
keyCharacteristics: An intaglio-green rail and jobs bar frame a stamp-paper ground; content lives on near-white sheets.
Every neutral is tinted from the green, so nothing on screen is plain grey.
Serial red is reserved for the run in flight.
Mono is used for every serial, count, ID and date, with tabular, slashed-zero figures.
Guilloché appears only in the rosette, the seal and the rail edge.

rules.name: The Serial Red Rule
rules.body: Serial red marks one thing only: a run that is in flight right now. A finished run's serial prints in ink-900 and its rosette in intaglio-800. Never use serial red for errors, emphasis or decoration.

rules.name: The Ochre Stays Dark Rule
rules.body: Ochre appears only on the intaglio surfaces (the rail, the seal and the jobs bar). It is never used as a fill or as text on a light sheet.

rules.name: The Tinted Neutral Rule
rules.body: Greys come from the ink ramp, which is tinted green. Plain Tailwind grey or slate is not part of this world.

rules.name: The Printed Number Rule
rules.body: Serials, counts, IDs, dates and durations are set in Red Hat Mono with tabular, slashed-zero figures. Words are set in Hanken.

rules.name: The Day-Month-Year Rule
rules.body: Dates read `06 Nov 2026`, and times are appended as `, 11:00`. Never use a locale-dependent or numeric-only date.

rules.name: The Paper Stack Rule
rules.body: Sheets separate from the ground by hairline and tone, not by shadow. If you can clearly see a shadow on a sheet at rest, it is too strong.

dos: Do frame every view with the intaglio-900 rail (or the mobile switcher) and the stamp ground. Content goes on sheet-coloured sheets with ink-200 hairlines.
Do print every serial, count, ID, date and duration in Red Hat Mono with tabular, slashed-zero figures.
Do keep one intaglio-900 primary button per view, for the committing action.
Do switch a run's serial and rosette from serial red to ink and intaglio the moment it stops being in flight.
Do use ochre-400 for focus and active markers on the dark surfaces, and intaglio-700 on light ones.
Do use dashed ink-300 borders for "nothing issued yet" and "in progress" states.
donts: Don't use serial red for anything except a run in flight. That rules out errors (use fault red), highlights and decoration.
Don't put guilloché anywhere except the rosette, the seal and the rail edge.
Don't use ochre on light sheets or as a button fill.
Don't introduce plain grey or slate neutrals, white page grounds or a blue accent.
Don't give sheets visible resting shadows. Only floating layers and the jobs bar are lifted.
Don't write dates in numeric or locale-dependent formats. Use `06 Nov 2026`.
